subject: math
title: 2D Shapes and 3D Objects: Faces, Edges, Vertices and Symmetry
seo_title: Grade 3 Math 2D Shapes and 3D Objects Worksheets: Prisms, Pyramids, Nets and Symmetry (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Sort and identify cubes, prisms, pyramids, cylinders, and cones by comparing their faces, edges, vertices, and angles
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 math worksheets on 2D shapes and 3D objects for the Ontario curriculum: name cubes, prisms, pyramids, cylinders and cones, count faces, edges and vertices, match nets, build and take apart shapes, and find lines of symmetry. 100 questions with an answer key, great for EQAO practice.
key_big: Count faces, edges and vertices to name an object. A pyramid comes to a point; a prism does not.
key_sub: Count the faces you cannot see too. A cylinder has 0 vertices. A line of symmetry makes 2 halves that match exactly when you fold.

faq.q: What 3D objects do Grade 3 students learn in Ontario?
faq.a: Cubes, prisms, pyramids, cylinders and cones. Students sort them by comparing their faces, edges, vertices and angles (Spatial Sense, expectation E1.1).

faq.q: How many faces, edges and vertices does a cylinder have?
faq.a: A cylinder has 2 flat circle faces and 1 curved surface, 2 curved edges and 0 vertices. It has no corners.

faq.q: Are shapes and symmetry on the Grade 3 EQAO math test?
faq.a: The Grade 3 EQAO math assessment is based on the Ontario curriculum, which includes Spatial Sense. Practising 3D objects, nets and matching halves helps students get ready.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn 3D objects and symmetry at home?
faq.a: Hunt for objects in the kitchen, like a soup can (cylinder) or a cereal box (rectangular prism), and count their faces, edges and vertices. Fold paper cut-outs to see if the halves match.

sets.title: Name 3D objects: cubes, prisms, pyramids, cylinders and cones

items.q: Name this 3D object.
items.e: It has 6 faces and they are all squares of the same size, so it is a cube. It is turned, but it is still a cube.
It has 1 flat circle face and a curved surface that comes to a point, so it is a cone. It is lying on its side, but it is still a cone.

items.q: What is this object called?
items.e: It has a square base and 4 triangle faces that meet at a point, so it is a square-based pyramid.

items.q: What is the name of this 3D object?
items.e: It has the same triangle at each end, joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. A prism does not come to a point. It is standing on a triangle face, but it is still a triangular prism.
It has 1 flat circle face and a curved surface that comes to a point, so it is a cone. It is upside down, but it is still a cone.
A is a rectangular prism: it has 6 rectangle faces that are not all squares. It is standing on its end.

items.q: What is the name of this 3D object?
items.e: It has a square base and 4 triangle faces that meet at a point, so it is a square-based pyramid. It is turned, but it is still a square-based pyramid.
C is a triangle-based pyramid: it has 4 triangle faces and comes to a point. The others have a square base, no point, or a curved surface.
B is a cone: it has 1 circle face and comes to a point. It is lying on its side.

items.q: Name this 3D object.
items.e: It has 4 triangle faces. It sits on a triangle base and the other 3 triangles meet at a point, so it is a triangle-based pyramid.

items.q: What is this object called?
items.e: It has 4 triangle faces. It sits on a triangle base and the other 3 triangles meet at a point, so it is a triangle-based pyramid. It is turned, but it is still a triangle-based pyramid.

items.q: What is the name of this 3D object?
items.e: It has 6 rectangle faces and they are not all squares, so it is a rectangular prism. It is standing on its end, but it is still a rectangular prism.

items.q: What is this object called?
items.e: It has 6 rectangle faces and they are not all squares, so it is a rectangular prism.

items.q: Name this 3D object.
items.e: It has the same triangle at each end, joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. A prism does not come to a point. It is turned so you see a triangle end at the front.

items.q: What is the name of this 3D object?
items.e: It has 6 faces and they are all squares of the same size, so it is a cube.

items.q: What is this object called?
items.e: It has the same triangle at each end, joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. A prism does not come to a point.
It has 2 flat circle faces and a curved surface, so it is a cylinder. A circle is only a flat 2D shape.
It has 1 flat circle face and a curved surface that comes to a point, so it is a cone.
It has 2 flat circle faces and a curved surface, so it is a cylinder. A circle is only a flat 2D shape. It is lying on its side, but it is still a cylinder.

items.q: Name this 3D object.
items.e: It has 6 rectangle faces and they are not all squares, so it is a rectangular prism. It is turned, but it is still a rectangular prism.

items.q: This is a triangle-based pyramid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangle-based pyramid has 4 faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: This is a rectangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: This is a cube. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too.

items.q: A corner of an object, where edges meet, is called a …
items.e: A corner is a vertex. More than one vertex are called vertices.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: Every face of a cube is a square. How many right angles does one face have?
items.e: A square has 4 square corners, so it has 4 right angles. 8 is the number of vertices of the whole cube.
A cylinder has no corners, so it has 0 vertices. Its 2 edges are curved circles, not corners. In a drawing it can look like it has 4 corners, but it does not.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too. Do not forget the vertex at the top.

items.q: The line where two faces of an object meet is called an …
items.e: Where two faces meet there is an edge.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: This is a cube. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too.

items.q: A flat surface of a 3D object is called a …
items.e: A face is a flat surface. An edge is where two faces meet. A vertex is a corner.

items.q: This is a rectangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: Which object has right angles at every corner of every face?
items.e: All 6 faces of a rectangular prism are rectangles, and every rectangle has 4 right angles. Pyramids and triangular prisms have triangle faces, and a triangle can never have a right angle at every corner.

items.q: This is a cube. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.
A cone has 1 vertex: the point at the top. Its circle edge is curved and has no corners.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: Noah says a cube has 8 edges. He is wrong. What did he count?
items.e: A cube has 8 vertices (corners) and 12 edges. Noah counted the vertices.

items.q: This net is folded up. Which 3D object does it make?
items.e: The 3 rectangles fold into a tube and the 2 triangles close the ends: a triangular prism.

items.q: This net is folded up. Which 3D object does it make?
items.e: 6 rectangles that are not all squares fold into a rectangular prism, like a box.

items.q: Which 2D shapes are the faces of a triangle-based pyramid?
items.e: It has 3 triangles that meet at the top and 1 more triangle as the base: 3 + 1 = 4 triangles. Do not forget the base.

items.q: Which 2D shapes are the faces of a triangular prism?
items.e: A triangular prism has a triangle at each end (2 triangles) and 3 rectangles joining them: 5 faces.

items.q: Which object can print 1 square and 4 triangles?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 1 square face and 4 triangle faces.

items.q: How many rectangle faces does a triangular prism have?
items.e: The 3 faces that join the 2 triangle ends are rectangles: 3 rectangles.

items.q: A net is a flat shape you can fold to make a 3D object. How many squares are in a net of a cube?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, so its net has 6 squares, one for each face. 8 is the number of vertices.

items.q: This net is folded up. Which 3D object does it make?
items.e: 6 squares of the same size fold up into a cube: 1 square for each face.

items.q: You press each face of an object in paint. Which object can print a triangle?
items.e: A triangular prism has a triangle face at each end. A cube, a cylinder and a rectangular prism have no triangle faces.

items.q: What shape is each face of a cube?
items.e: All 6 faces of a cube are squares of the same size. A cube is the 3D object; its faces are 2D squares.

items.q: Which 2D shapes are the faces of a rectangular prism like a cereal box?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces and each one is a rectangle: front and back, top and bottom, and 2 ends.

items.q: What shape is the flat face of a cone?
items.e: A cone has 1 flat face: a circle. From the side a cone looks like a triangle, but it has no triangle faces.

items.q: How many triangle faces does a triangular prism have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 1 triangle at each end: 2 triangles. Its name says “triangle”, but its other 3 faces are rectangles.

items.q: Which 2D shapes are the faces of a square-based pyramid?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 1 square at the bottom and 4 triangles that meet at the top: 5 faces.

items.q: This net is folded up. Which 3D object does it make?
items.e: The square is the base. The 4 triangles fold up and meet at a point: a square-based pyramid.
The flat faces of a cylinder are circles. In a drawing they look like ovals because we see them from the side.

items.q: Emma dips one face of a cube in paint and presses it on paper. What shape does she print?
items.e: Every face of a cube is a square, so the print is a square. A print is flat (2D), so it cannot be a cube.

items.q: How many square faces does a square-based pyramid have?
items.e: Only the base is a square: 1 square face. The other 4 faces are triangles.

items.q: This net is folded up. Which 3D object does it make?
items.e: The rectangle rolls into a tube (the curved surface) and the 2 circles close the ends: a cylinder.

items.q: Leah traces around the bottom of a soup can. What shape does she draw?
items.e: The can is a cylinder and its bottom face is a circle, so the tracing is a circle.

sets.title: Build and take apart: shapes and objects

items.q: How many triangles make this hexagon?
items.e: Count the triangles around the centre: 6. A hexagon has 6 sides, and each side belongs to one triangle.

items.q: Ava cuts a cube of cheese straight down, from one corner of the top to the opposite corner. What 2 objects does she get?
items.e: The cut makes a triangle at the top and a triangle at the bottom of each piece, joined by rectangles. Each piece is a triangular prism. It does not come to a point, so it is not a pyramid.

items.q: You put 2 squares of the same size side by side. Which shape do you make?
items.e: 2 squares side by side make a rectangle twice as long as it is wide. It has 4 sides, not 4 + 4 = 8.

items.q: Which shapes make this rectangle?
items.e: The line in the middle cuts the rectangle into 2 equal squares.

items.q: You put 2 cubes side by side and glue them together. Which 3D object do you make?
items.e: The new object has 6 faces: 2 squares at the ends and 4 long rectangles. It is a rectangular prism, not a cube.

c: a cylinder and a square-based pyramid
items.e: The tall part has 2 circle faces and a curved side: a cylinder. The roof has a circle base and a point: a cone. A rectangle and a triangle are flat 2D shapes.

items.q: Which shapes make this square?
items.e: The line goes from one corner to the opposite corner. It cuts the square into 2 triangles.

items.q: Which shapes make this trapezoid?
items.e: Count the pieces: 3 triangles. With pattern blocks, 3 triangle blocks make 1 trapezoid block.

items.q: Lucas cuts a rectangle from one corner to the opposite corner. What two shapes does he get?
items.e: A cut from corner to corner makes 2 triangles. A cut across the middle would make 2 rectangles.

items.q: This model house is made of two 3D objects. Which two?
c: a rectangular prism and a triangular prism
a rectangular prism and a square-based pyramid
items.e: The bottom has 6 rectangle faces: a rectangular prism. The roof has a triangle at each end and does not come to a point: a triangular prism.

items.q: Which shape is made from a square and a triangle?
items.e: D is a square with a triangle on top. The others are a rectangle and a triangle, a trapezoid and a triangle, and 2 triangles.

items.q: This tower is made of two 3D objects. Which two?
c: a cube and a triangular prism
a cube and a square-based pyramid
items.e: The bottom has 6 square faces: a cube. The top has 4 triangle faces that meet at a point: a square-based pyramid. A cone has a circle base.

items.q: How many sides does the outline of the whole house have?
items.e: Go around the outside: 2 walls, the floor and 2 roof sides = 5 sides, so the outline is a pentagon. Do not add 4 + 3 = 7: the line where the roof meets the wall is inside.

items.q: Which shapes make this rocket?
items.e: The body is a rectangle. The nose is a triangle and there is a triangle fin on each side: 1 + 2 = 3 triangles.

items.q: Which shapes make this L shape?
items.e: A tall rectangle and a flat rectangle make the L. Neither piece has 4 equal sides, so they are not squares.

items.q: Which two shapes make this tree?
items.e: The top of the tree is a triangle and the trunk is a thin rectangle.

items.q: Which two shapes make this house?
items.e: The wall is a square (4 equal sides) and the roof is a triangle (3 sides).

items.q: Which shapes make this hexagon?
items.e: The line cuts the hexagon into 2 pieces. Each piece has 4 sides and 1 pair of parallel sides, so each is a trapezoid.

items.q: Liam cuts a cube of cheese straight down the middle into 2 equal halves. What 2 objects does he get?
items.e: Each half has 6 faces: 2 squares and 4 rectangles that are not squares. So each half is a rectangular prism. Half a cube is not a cube.

items.q: Which two shapes make this arrow?
items.e: The long part is a rectangle and the point is a triangle.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry?
c: Yes, it cuts the shape into 2 parts.
No, a line of symmetry must go up and down.
No, the two halves do not match.
items.e: The top half is narrower than the bottom half, so the halves do not match when you fold.

items.q: Look at the lines painted on a soccer field from above. How many lines of symmetry do they have?
items.e: The two halves of the field match across the halfway line, and the left and right sides match along the long middle line: 2 lines.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry?
c: No, the two halves do not match.
No, a line of symmetry must go up and down.
Yes, it cuts the shape into 2 parts.
items.e: Fold along the line: the slanted sides go opposite ways, so the halves do not match.

items.q: Priya cuts a paper snowflake with 6 arms that are all the same. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: A line of symmetry can go through each arm. A snowflake with 6 matching arms has 6 lines of symmetry.

items.q: Mei folds a paper in half and cuts half a heart along the fold. She opens the paper. Where is the line of symmetry of the heart?
c: across the middle, from side to side
items.e: The fold is the line of symmetry. The cut makes the same edge on both halves, so the halves match along the fold.

items.q: Which picture shows a line of symmetry?
items.e: A shows a line of symmetry: the rectangle is folded exactly in half. The other lines make halves that do not match.

items.q: Which capital letter has a line of symmetry going across, from side to side?
items.e: Fold E across the middle: the top half matches the bottom half. A has a line going up and down, not across. N and R have none.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry?
c: Yes, it cuts the shape into 2 parts.
No, a line of symmetry must go side to side.
No, the two halves do not match.
items.e: Fold along the line: the left half lands exactly on the right half.

items.q: Hana has a rectangle card that is not a square. In how many ways can she fold it so the halves match exactly?
items.e: Hana can fold it top to bottom or side to side: 2 ways. A fold from corner to corner does not match on a rectangle.

items.q: This triangle has 3 equal sides. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: Each line goes from a corner to the middle of the opposite side. There are 3 corners, so there are 3 lines of symmetry.

items.q: Which capital letter has matching halves when you fold it down the middle, from top to bottom?
items.e: Fold T down the middle: the left half matches the right half. F, G and J do not have matching halves.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry?
c: No, the two halves do not match.
Yes, it cuts the shape into 2 parts.
No, a line of symmetry must go up and down.
items.e: Fold the square from corner to corner: the 2 triangles match exactly. A line of symmetry can go any way, even on a slant.

items.q: Chloe draws the left half of a maple leaf next to a mirror line. How should the right half look?
c: the same shape, slid over without flipping
the same shape, flipped like a mirror
a bigger copy of the left half
items.e: Matching halves are mirror images. The right half is the left half flipped over the line, not slid across.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry?
c: Yes, it cuts the shape into 2 parts.
No, a line of symmetry must go up and down.
No, the two halves do not match.
items.e: Fold along the line: the top half lands exactly on the bottom half. Lines of symmetry can go side to side too.

items.q: A stop sign is a shape with 8 equal sides. Forget the words on it. How many lines of symmetry does the shape have?
items.e: A shape with 8 equal sides and 8 equal angles has 8 lines of symmetry: 4 through opposite corners and 4 through the middles of opposite sides.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry?
c: No, the two halves do not match.
Yes, it cuts the shape into 2 parts.
No, a line of symmetry must go up and down.
items.e: Fold a rectangle from corner to corner and the corners stick out: the halves do not match. The line cuts it into 2 triangles of the same size, but they do not match when you fold.

items.q: Which picture shows a line of symmetry?
items.e: D shows a line of symmetry: the 2 halves match when you fold. The other lines cut the shape in two, but the halves do not match.

items.q: The dashed line is a mirror line. The dot is 3 squares to the left of the line. Where is the matching dot?
c: 3 squares to the right of the line
6 squares to the right of the line
1 square to the right of the line
items.e: A matching point is the same distance from the mirror line, on the other side: 3 squares to the left, so 3 squares to the right. 1 comes from counting from the edge of the grid.

items.q: Think of the flag of Canada. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: Fold the flag down the middle: the red bands and the two halves of the maple leaf match. Fold it across and the leaf does not match upside down, so there is only 1 line of symmetry.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
items.e: A square has 4 lines of symmetry: 1 up and down, 1 side to side and 2 from corner to corner. Do not forget the 2 slanted lines.
